reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because its primary purpose is an instructional cooking demonstration about preparing ginger and green chilli paste. The discussion of refrigerator or freezer storage is food-preparation guidance, and the request to like, share, subscribe, and comment is ordinary audience engagement rather than a request for money, credentials, or financial participation.

citations.quote: today I am going to share with you the fine ginger & green chili paste
To make this paste, you need look for this type of chilli in bottle
keep it in cold water for 10-15 mins and make paste
Now we'll put this in airtight container. Our paste is ready.
If you like my recipe then please Like, Share this video and Subscribe to my Channel

opening.argument: The video pairs a finished preparation with a direct request for audience action: viewers are told to like, share, subscribe, and comment after being shown a supposedly useful paste that can be reused in many dishes. That combination can be read as a low-barrier solicitation for engagement in exchange for access to a claimed practical benefit. The evidence does not establish a monetary reward, but the action-benefit linkage is still the closest fit to a simple acquisition funnel: perform the requested actions, then gain the recipe and claimed culinary utility.

citations.quote: If you like my recipe then please Like, Share this video and Subscribe to my Channel Also, please click the bell icon
If you have this paste, then you can make any type of recipe.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the video an instructional demonstration does not answer the solicitation itself. The speaker does not merely present ingredients; she explicitly asks viewers to like, share, subscribe, click the bell, and comment. That directed sequence can promote participation and audience growth, while the claimed usefulness of the paste supplies the inducement. The fact that the requested action is social-media engagement rather than payment does not eliminate the possibility of deceptive low-barrier acquisition.

citations.quote: please Like, Share this video and Subscribe to my Channel Also, please click the bell icon
Try this recipe and let us know in comments How was the recipe?

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The requested actions are ordinary channel-engagement requests, not a promised reward, withdrawal, asset, or income payment. The cited benefit is simply culinary information: the speaker says the paste can be used in recipes, while the method consists of chilling, blending, and storing ingredients. Nothing in these quotes shows that liking, sharing, or subscribing unlocks money or a valuable digital or physical asset.

citations.quote: If you have this paste, then you can make any type of recipe.
keep it in cold water for 10-15 mins and make paste
please Like, Share this video and Subscribe to my Channel

opening.argument: Several claims could encourage viewers to act quickly or rely on the preparation: the speaker describes the chilli as very hot but tasty, says the paste is initially very spicy, and gives unusually specific longevity claims of 15 to 20 days refrigerated and two months frozen while promising it will retain its color. Those assurances make the preparation sound broadly useful and low-risk. Although no financial return is stated, the combination of strong benefit language and preservation assurances leaves open a low-barrier promotional acquisition claim rather than proving the content is harmless.

citations.quote: This chili is very hot If we add little chili, It becomes really tasty
When we prepare paste first or second day, it will be very spicy And when it gets to old, it will become mild
this paste will last for 15 to 20 days
If you deep freeze it, it will last for 2 months

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats storage advice as neutral without addressing how prominently the video emphasizes durability and preserved appearance. Statements that the paste lasts for weeks or months and will not turn black can make the result appear especially reliable and broadly useful. Even without an explicit payment request, such assurances may strengthen a low-barrier inducement to follow the creator and adopt the promoted preparation.

citations.quote: this paste will last for 15 to 20 days
If you deep freeze it, it will last for 2 months
it will stay in the same color and will not turn black

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are food-storage and taste statements, not returns, rewards, or asset-acquisition promises. The speaker explains that the paste becomes milder with age and describes placing it in an airtight container. The cited claims may be assessed for culinary accuracy, but they do not connect any reward or valuable asset to clicking, registering, depositing, buying, or inviting others.

citations.quote: And when it gets to old, it will become mild
Now we'll put this in airtight container. Our paste is ready.

opening.argument: The apparent cooking lesson also functions as promotion for the creator and channel. The presenter introduces herself and the channel, repeatedly frames the paste as useful across many preparations, displays the finished product, and closes by requesting likes, shares, subscriptions, bell activation, and comments. That structure steers viewers toward continued participation rather than merely conveying a recipe. The closest scam classification is a low-barrier acquisition pathway: viewers are encouraged to perform simple actions while being promised practical value and broad usefulness.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cooking format does not negate its promotional function. The presenter identifies the channel, emphasizes that one paste supports many dishes, shows the completed product, and then asks for several forms of audience participation. Those elements can steer viewers into a continuing engagement path. The absence of a payment request narrows the allegation, but does not by itself rule out deceptive low-barrier solicitation.

Those facts show promotion in the ordinary media sense, but they do not show a reward, financial opportunity, external claim flow, or valuable asset tied to participation.
